bill.title: A resolution designating May 10, 2025, as "World Migratory Bird Day".
bill.latestActionText: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S2831; text: CR S2843)
bill.officialSummary: This resolution designates May 10, 2025, as World Migratory Bird Day.

classification.plainSummary:
This resolution designates May 10, 2025, as World Migratory Bird Day.

This is a measure the Library of Congress labels as a congressional tribute or commemoration. It carries no sector tags and no donor overlap is computed for it, because attributing an economic interest to a commemorative or procedural measure would be misleading.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would name May 10, 2025, as World Migratory Bird Day.
plain.whoItTouches: People living near whatever is being regulated.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in the air, water and land where you live. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
